learningObjective: Understand how AOTInductor artifacts behave at runtime with respect to dynamic shapes and shape mismatch.

canonicalClaims.claim: An AOTInductor artifact contains compiled kernels + a runtime wrapper; loading and running it does not re-invoke torch.compile, and shape-constraint violations at runtime raise errors rather than trigger recompilation. Dims not declared dynamic must match the export-time example exactly.
conditions: The user declared dynamic dims via Dim constraints at export.
nonImplications: Does not imply the artifact is portable across GPU vendors or CPU/GPU boundaries.
Does not imply that unconstrained dims are handled dynamically.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor transparently migrates execution to the runtime device.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The artifact targets compile-time hardware; no cross-device migration is provided.

misconceptions.claim: Dims not declared dynamic are also flexible at runtime.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Undeclared dims are treated as static.

misconceptions.claim: Shape violations trigger a fresh torch.compile at runtime.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The artifact is AOT; the runtime does not re-invoke torch.compile.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor artifacts always contain a Python interpreter for control flow.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The artifact is native code + a small wrapper; no Python interpreter is bundled.

implementationFacts: Dim constraints translate to runtime shape assertions in the wrapper
Device targeting is set at compile time
performanceScenarios: AOTInductor is used to eliminate cold-start compile latency in production deployments.
